    Paths in ray residue categories #

    Lift the reversed irreducible quiver of a proper zero-ideal quotient back to the original ray category. This is the path-level transport needed in the residue induction of BGRS 8.6.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ZeroHomIdeal.not_mem_left_of_comp_not_mem {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] (I : ZeroHomIdeal C) {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hfg : ¬I.mem (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g)) :
    ¬I.mem f

    If a composite lies outside a zero Hom ideal, then its first factor lies outside the ideal.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.ZeroHomIdeal.not_mem_right_of_comp_not_mem {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] (I : ZeroHomIdeal C) {X Y Z : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (hfg : ¬I.mem (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp f g)) :
    ¬I.mem g

    If a composite lies outside a zero Hom ideal, then its second factor lies outside the ideal.

                                              One complete residue-induction step. Exactness of the restricted quotient contour function first supplies a lifted correction which makes the original function cling to every surviving ray. A local invisible correction then adds the distinguished killed ray without disturbing any survivor. The two successive corrections are combined into one arrow-weight family.

                                              def LargeIndecomposable.ZeroHomIdeal.HasInvisibleCorrectionClingingOnIdeal {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms C] {k : Type u_1} [Field k] (J : ZeroHomIdeal C) :
                                              Prop

                                              The ideal-level local correction obligation. Besides being invisible on all surviving essential contours, the correction makes the contour function cling to every nonzero path annihilated by the ideal. For the principal ideal of a maximal ray, the annihilated nonzero paths all represent exactly that one ray.
